Visual Analysis: This is a grouped bar chart titled 'Public Records Requests Received vs. Closed Within 21 Days (excluding LexisNexis & MRB)'. The chart displays data for monthly periods from July 2018 to June 2019. The vertical axis represents the number of requests, ranging from 0 to 1000. The horizontal axis lists the months. For each month, two bars are shown: a dark blue bar representing 'Requests received' and a teal bar representing 'Requests closed in 21 days or fewer'. The data reveals that the number of requests received each month consistently exceeded 600, with peaks in October 2018, January 2019, and April 2019. The number of requests closed within 21 days was significantly lower, ranging from approximately 200 to 500, with a notable increase in June 2019. The chart visually demonstrates a persistent gap between the volume of incoming requests and the rate at which they are processed within the 21-day target. The chart's design is clean and functional, using a grid for easy reading and distinct colors for clarity. The data is presented in a context of public records management, specifically for the Portland Police Bureau's Records Division, which aims to respond to 95% of requests within 21 calendar days. The chart highlights the challenge of meeting this goal, as only 39% of requests were closed within the target timeframe during FY 2018-19, with the chart showing the monthly breakdown of this performance.

nodes.text: The division made several process improvements over the course of FY 2018-19, including process mapping to identify efficiencies, improving the accuracy of submissions from highvolume requestors, and switching to faster browsers. Additional improvements are planned, including the implementation of a planned interface between GovQA and the Police Bureau’s records management system. For smaller potential improvements, the division is taking the laudable approach of testing and evaluating efficiency proposals to identify the cost/benefit ratio before rolling out unit-wide.

nodes.title: Prior Year Performance Report  Promoting a Transparent, Effective, Engaged Government  Community Member Touchpoints with Government
nodes.text: The City Attorney’s office and BTS have worked to improve response times during the GovQA system implementation and subsequent enhancements. The PROActive Pages feature in GovQA allows the City to post information on trending topics so that interested parties can access those high-profile records quickly and at no additional cost. This reduces City staff time responding to multiple requests for the same information. Currently, neither bureau reports on performance measures related to public records requests, such as

nodes.text: CBO recommends that the City continue efforts to track the total time and cost related to each public records request. Currently, GovQA tracks response times and cost for requests that go through that system. For requests that go directly through bureaus, tracking varies. The City Attorney’s Office is currently working to improve bureau tracking. As the City continues to automate the process and reduce time spent on research and response, measuring the volume, timeliness, and cost of fulfilling public records requests will help quantify the benefits of process improvements and ensure that the most effective practices can be replicated.

nodes.text: Permitting Turnaround Times

nodes.title: Prior Year Performance Report  Promoting a Transparent, Effective, Engaged Government  Community Member Touchpoints with Government
nodes.text: The Bureau of Development Services (BDS) issues permits for construction and renovation of commercial and residential buildings. Through BDS’ and other bureaus’ reviews of permit applications, the City ensures that buildings are safe and that their uses are in line with the City’s land use plans.

nodes.title: Prior Year Performance Report  Promoting a Transparent, Effective, Engaged Government  Community Member Touchpoints with Government
nodes.text: BDS has made efforts in recent years to shorten turnaround times for permitting, review, and inspection tasks or processes to facilitate a better customer experience. The FY 2018-19 performance measures highlighted below show improved turnaround times for commercial plan and permitting reviews and inspections, as well as for land use reviews. While some of these efficiency gains can be attributed to reduced development activity in FY 2018-19, some of the improvements may have arisen from process improvement efforts and active monitoring of these measures.

nodes.title: Prior Year Performance Report  Promoting a Transparent, Effective, Engaged Government  Community Member Touchpoints with Government
nodes.text: Residential permitting process timelines performed less well. BDS (and other development bureaus) ended FY 2018-19 having reviewed only $66 \%$ of residential plans within scheduled end dates, short of the $72 \%$ target and slightly lower than the previous year’s $68 \%$ . BDS notes that while they are responsible for coordinating and monitoring development review, timeliness depends on all seven bureaus involved in review.3 Last year, the bureaus or programs taking the longest for residential plan review were the Portland Bureau of Transportation, the Water Bureau, and the Life Safety review group within BDS.

The chart is presented on a white background with black text and gridlines, using a clean, professional style. The context from surrounding text indicates this chart is part of a report analyzing BDS's performance in FY 2018-19, highlighting improvements in commercial permitting and noting that residential permitting timelines performed less well, falling short of the 72% target.

nodes.title: Prior Year Performance Report  Promoting a Transparent, Effective, Engaged Government  Community Member Touchpoints with Government
nodes.text: Development bureaus have tried different strategies to improve the development review process over the past several years. Mayor Wheeler led a series of Government Accountability, Transparency and Results (GATR) performance management sessions on Housing Development4 from 2016-2018, and created the “Fast Track” program to test new approaches to high-priority projects. The Development Directors' Group was established in December 2017 to improve development services results. In FY 2019-20, the seven development bureaus are undertaking a strategic planning process focused on improving coordination, transparency, and decision-making during plan review. In September 2019, BDS executed a contract with a consultant, Catalysis LLC, to facilitate the process, and a steering committee of representatives from the bureaus had its kick-off meeting in October.

nodes.title: Prior Year Performance Report  Promoting a Transparent, Effective, Engaged Government  Community Member Touchpoints with Government
nodes.text: The Portland Online Permitting System (POPS) project, when implemented, is expected to significantly improve the review process, allowing the full permitting process to happen online, with different bureaus conducting their reviews simultaneously. In FY 2018-19, BDS made progress on the development and implementation of several POPS components and noted that having the ability to review plans electronically has resulted in the shortening of the time for submitting and reviewing project revisions from hours to minutes. The bureau anticipates further efficiencies to come from the implementation of additional components of the project in FY 2019-20, including the launch of the AMANDA permitting software upgrade in February 2020.

nodes.text: 311 Update

nodes.title: Prior Year Performance Report  Promoting a Transparent, Effective, Engaged Government  Community Member Touchpoints with Government
nodes.text: The FY 2019-20 Adopted Budget includes funding for the implementation of a Citywide 311 system. The purpose of the 311 program is to improve Citywide customer service by: offering a first stop for community questions or requests online, in person, and over the phone; hiring diverse staff; improving and better integrating language services; and conducting outreach and education about the program to historically underserved community members.

nodes.title: Prior Year Performance Report  Promoting a Transparent, Effective, Engaged Government  Community Member Touchpoints with Government
nodes.text: City Council recently passed Resolution 37456 formally creating the program, merging the existing Information and Referral (I&R) program with 311, and moving the program from the Office of Community and Civic Life (Civic Life) to the Chief Administrative Officer’s office within the Office of Management & Finance (OMF). The Resolution approved a budget increase to an estimated fully-funded total of $\$ 3.1$ million. OMF will work to create performance measures in the coming years to track the program’s success, but the program will not be fully implemented until FY 2022-23. CBO encourages the program to set interim performance measures for the period before full implementation.

nodes.section: Procurement Division: Process Improvements and Expansion
nodes.text: The City of Portland Procurement Services is a vital City function, serving as an intermediary between bureaus and the market for contracts totaling about $\$ 500$ million annually. Procurement Services plays a critical role in the implementation timeline for projects and programming across the City and is responsible for advancing the City’s goals to support social equity in contracting practices.

These SLAs were newly established in FY 2018-19, marking a significant shift from prior practices where cycle times were not tracked. The table supports the surrounding context by illustrating the Procurement Division’s commitment to transparency and performance measurement, as it now benchmarks procurement efficiency against specific targets. The data also contextualizes the division’s success: only 9 out of total processes missed SLA targets (8 for Construction Invitation to Bid and 1 for Goods & Services RFP), validating the effectiveness of these new metrics. The table directly relates to the broader city-wide efforts to improve turnaround times, including BDS’s performance measures and POPS implementation, by showing how procurement—often a bottleneck—has been formalized with measurable goals. The SLAs also reflect the reorganization of Procurement Services, including the creation of a Design and Construction Services team, and align with the strategic planning underway across development bureaus to enhance coordination and decision-making. The table thus serves as a foundational performance baseline for future improvements and accountability, enabling the Procurement Division to track progress against its equity and efficiency goals.

nodes.text: Procurement also created a stand-alone Design and Construction Services team with seven additional FTE in preparation for a projected increase in capital outlay across infrastructure bureaus. This was funded through interagency agreements with infrastructure bureaus with regular construction contracts, which includes: the Bureau of Transportation, BDS, Parks and Recreation, Bureau of Environmental Services, Water Bureau, Spectator Facilities, Facilities Services, BTS, Fire Bureau, and Civic Life. Visual Analysis: This bar chart, titled 'FY 2018-19 Procurement Service Level Agreement', visually compares the Service Level Agreement (SLA) targets against the actual cycle times for five distinct procurement processes. The vertical axis represents 'Calendar Days', ranging from 0 to 350. Each process is represented by two adjacent bars: a yellow bar for the SLA target and a blue bar for the actual performance. The processes, from left to right, are: 'Construction Invitation to Bid' (SLA: 168 days, Actual: 101 days), 'Goods & Services Request for Proposals' (SLA: 308 days, Actual: 161 days), 'Goods & Services Invitation to Bid' (SLA: 108 days, Actual: 27 days), 'Professional, Technical, Expert Request for Proposal' (SLA: 274 days, Actual: 120 days), and 'Professional, Technical, Expert Direct Contract' (SLA: 122 days, Actual: 31 days). The chart demonstrates that, for all five categories, the actual cycle times were significantly shorter than the SLA targets, indicating successful performance against the established benchmarks for that fiscal year. The visual style is clean and corporate, using a simple color scheme of yellow and blue against a white background with gray gridlines. The chart is presented in the context of a report on the City of Portland's Procurement Division, which introduced these SLAs in FY 2018-19 as a major improvement to track and reduce procurement cycle times, a change that was previously unmeasured. The data shown provides a performance baseline for future reporting and improvement efforts.

nodes.text: Adjust Performance Targets

nodes.title: Prior Year Performance Report  Promoting a Transparent, Effective, Engaged Government  Community Member Touchpoints with Government
nodes.text: Due to inconsistent historical practices in the various procurement groups and the use of disparate data systems, establishing a true baseline for service level agreements was a challenge. The general consensus among stakeholders and Procurement was that the cycle timeline goals were modest and were likely to be met in the first year. CBO urges the division to refine its targets to ensure they reflect ambitious cycle times that represent improved customer service. Procurement Services has stated that is currently analyzing prior year performance data to refine performance goals by procurement type for the next fiscal year.

nodes.title: Prior Year Performance Report  Promoting a Transparent, Effective, Engaged Government  Community Member Touchpoints with Government
nodes.text: Data Consistency

nodes.title: Prior Year Performance Report  Promoting a Transparent, Effective, Engaged Government  Community Member Touchpoints with Government
nodes.text: There are some noted issues with data consistency in this first iteration of performance tracking, including the appearance of negative cycle times. The division states that there is inconsistency in the way buyers currently enter data into the BuySpeed system, which causes errors in calculation of cycle times. There are also issues in the numbers for the Goods and Services Invitation to Bid Contracts process. The prior year actuals show a 27-day average cycle time, which is significantly lower than the SLA of 108. The division stated that this is due to a data management issue in the Procurement Software Application; it is currently including all Goods and Services Invitation to Bid Contracts, but the SLA was set only for contracts over $\$ 50,000$ , which follow a different process than those under $\$ 50,000$ . CBO anticipates continued efforts to ensure consistency from Procurement Services, as well as ensuring that documentation about data quality is available to both customer bureaus and to the public.

nodes.title: Prior Year Performance Report  Promoting a Transparent, Effective, Engaged Government  Community Member Touchpoints with Government
nodes.text: Cycle Time Tracking

nodes.title: Prior Year Performance Report  Promoting a Transparent, Effective, Engaged Government  Community Member Touchpoints with Government
nodes.text: Several customer bureaus have given feedback that they often experience delays during the Procurement intake process. These delays, due to submission errors or miscommunication, are not reflected in Procurement’s performance reporting. Although “complete and accurate transmittal” is stated in the SLA as a bureau responsibility, CBO recommends that Procurement Services evaluate whether additional performance measures that track the full cycle time would be beneficial, and if increased training for bureau staff on submission issues may be necessary.

nodes.title: Prior Year Performance Report  Promoting a Transparent, Effective, Engaged Government  Community Member Touchpoints with Government
nodes.text: Procurement Services plans to continue process improvements in this arena, such as establishing SLAs for the procurement processes that were not included in its initial effort and assessing metrics and interactions with bureau customers to continue to find opportunities to improve.

nodes.text: 5. Arming the System

nodes.title: BOSCH  Copyright Notice  New Zealand Telepermit Notes
nodes.text: There are several ways to arm the system depending on whether you are:

nodes.title: BOSCH  Copyright Notice  New Zealand Telepermit Notes
nodes.text: Leaving the premises and require all active zones to be in a ready state for an intruder. Remaining in the premises and only require part of the system to be in a ready state for an intruder.

nodes.title: BOSCH  Copyright Notice  New Zealand Telepermit Notes
nodes.text: If a zone is not sealed at the end of exit time, the zone is automatically isolated and constantly displays on the remote codepad. The zone becomes an active part of the system when the zone reseals. For example, if a window is left open after exit time expires, the window is not an active part of the system until the window is closed. Opening the window after exit time expired causes an alarm condition.

Each mode corresponds to a specific operational context — AWAY Mode for full system arming when leaving premises, STAY Mode 1 for partial arming with installer-defined isolated zones, and STAY Mode 2 for partial arming with user-defined isolated zones. nodes.text: Forced Arming

nodes.title: BOSCH  Copyright Notice  New Zealand Telepermit Notes
nodes.text: The feature of arming the system when a zone is not sealed is known as forced arming. If the system does not arm and a long beep is heard, forced arming is not permitted. If this is the case, ensure that all zones are sealed or manually isolated before arming the system.

nodes.title: BOSCH  Copyright Notice  New Zealand Telepermit Notes
nodes.text: 5.1 Arming in AWAY Mode

nodes.title: BOSCH  Copyright Notice  New Zealand Telepermit Notes
nodes.text: When you leave your premises and require all zones to be in a ready state to detect intrusion, you arm the system in AWAY Mode. When returning to your premises, disarm your system (see Section 6. Disarming the System) so you do not sound a false alarm.

nodes.title: BOSCH  Copyright Notice  New Zealand Telepermit Notes
nodes.text: There are two different methods for arming the system in AWAY Mode. Method one is standard and always operates. Method two is optional and may be disabled by your installer if you do not want to use single button arming.

nodes.title: BOSCH  Copyright Notice  New Zealand Telepermit Notes
nodes.text: Arming in AWAY Mode, Method 1

nodes.title: BOSCH  Copyright Notice  New Zealand Telepermit Notes
nodes.text: Enter your user code followed by the [#] key (for example, [2 5 8 0 #]). Two beeps sound and the AWAY indicator displays. Exit time starts counting.

nodes.title: BOSCH  Copyright Notice  New Zealand Telepermit Notes
nodes.text: Arming in AWAY Mode, Method 2

nodes.title: BOSCH  Copyright Notice  New Zealand Telepermit Notes
nodes.text: Hold down the [#] key until two beeps sound. The AWAY indicator displays and exit time starts counting.

nodes.title: BOSCH  Copyright Notice  New Zealand Telepermit Notes
nodes.text: 5.2 Arming in STAY Mode 1

nodes.title: BOSCH  Copyright Notice  New Zealand Telepermit Notes
nodes.text: STAY Mode 1 is only used when the perimeter and unused areas of the premises must be armed to detect if an intruder is entering the premises. At the same time it allows you to move freely within an area that is automatically isolated.

nodes.title: BOSCH  Copyright Notice  New Zealand Telepermit Notes
nodes.text: Only your security company can program zones automatically isolated in STAY Mode 1.

nodes.title: BOSCH  Copyright Notice  New Zealand Telepermit Notes
nodes.text: There are two different methods for arming the system in STAY Mode 1. Method one is standard and always operates. Method two is optional and may be disabled by your installer if you do not want to use single button arming.

nodes.title: BOSCH  Copyright Notice  New Zealand Telepermit Notes
nodes.section: Entry Guard Timer for STAY Mode 1
nodes.text: Entry Guard Timer for STAY Mode 1

nodes.title: BOSCH  Copyright Notice  New Zealand Telepermit Notes
nodes.section: Entry Guard Timer for STAY Mode 1
nodes.text: When arming the system in STAY Mode 1, an optional entry timer called Entry Guard Timer For STAY Mode 1 is available. Use this entry timer to delay the sirens if a zone is not automatically isolated and triggers an alarm condition. Entry Guard Timer For STAY Mode 1 is the delay time used for all zones except 24-hour zones when the system is armed in STAY Mode 1 or STAY Mode 2.

nodes.title: BOSCH  Copyright Notice  New Zealand Telepermit Notes
nodes.section: Entry Guard Timer for STAY Mode 1
nodes.text: If the Entry Guard Timer For STAY Mode 1 is programmed and a zone not automatically isolated is triggered, the codepad beeps twice per second until the entry timer expires or the system disarms. If the alarm condition is not reset by entering your user code followed by the [#] key (for example, [2 5 8 0 #]) before the entry timer expires, the sirens activate into alarm. Only your installer can program this feature.

nodes.title: BOSCH  Copyright Notice  New Zealand Telepermit Notes
nodes.text: Arming in STAY Mode 1, Method 1

nodes.title: BOSCH  Copyright Notice  New Zealand Telepermit Notes
nodes.text: Enter your user code followed by the [\*] key (for example, $\left[ 2 5 8 0 ^ { * } \right]$ ). Two beeps sound and the STAY indicator displays. Exit time starts counting.

nodes.title: BOSCH  Copyright Notice  New Zealand Telepermit Notes
nodes.text: Any zones programmed to be automatically isolated in STAY Mode 1 flash until exit time expires. At the end of exit time, all zones selected to be automatically isolated turn off and the codepad gives one short beep.

nodes.title: BOSCH  Copyright Notice  New Zealand Telepermit Notes
nodes.text: Arming in STAY Mode 1, Method 2

nodes.title: BOSCH  Copyright Notice  New Zealand Telepermit Notes
nodes.text: Hold down the [\*] button until two beeps are heard. The STAY indicator displays and exit time starts counting.

nodes.title: BOSCH  Copyright Notice  New Zealand Telepermit Notes
nodes.text: Any zones programmed to be automatically isolated in STAY Mode 1 flash until exit time expires. At the end of exit time, the zone indicators turn off and the codepad emits one short beep.

nodes.title: BOSCH  Copyright Notice  New Zealand Telepermit Notes
nodes.text: 5.3 Arming in STAY Mode 2

nodes.title: BOSCH  Copyright Notice  New Zealand Telepermit Notes
nodes.text: STAY Mode 2 is only used when the perimeter and unused areas of the premises must be armed to detect an intruder from entering the premises while you move freely within an area that is automatically isolated. Any Master Code user can program zones to be automatically isolated in STAY Mode 2.

nodes.title: BOSCH  Copyright Notice  New Zealand Telepermit Notes
nodes.section: Entry Guard Timer For STAY Mode 2
nodes.text: Entry Guard Timer For STAY Mode 2

nodes.title: BOSCH  Copyright Notice  New Zealand Telepermit Notes
nodes.section: Entry Guard Timer For STAY Mode 2
nodes.text: When arming the system in STAY Mode 2, an optional entry timer called Entry Guard Timer For STAY Mode 2 is available. Use this entry timer to delay the sirens if a zone is not automatically isolated and triggered into alarm condition. Entry Guard Timer for STAY Mode 2 is the delay time used for all zones except 24-hour zones when the system is armed in STAY Mode 1 or STAY Mode 2.

nodes.title: BOSCH  Copyright Notice  New Zealand Telepermit Notes
nodes.section: Entry Guard Timer For STAY Mode 2
nodes.text: If the Entry Guard Timer For STAY Mode 2 is programmed and a zone not automatically isolated triggers, the codepad beeps twice a second until the entry timer expires or the system disarms. If the alarm condition is not reset by entering your user code followed by the [#] button (for example, $\left[ 2 \ 5 \ 8 \ 0 \ \# \right] ,$ ) before the entry timer expires, the sirens activate into alarm. Only your installer can program this option.

nodes.title: BOSCH  Copyright Notice  New Zealand Telepermit Notes
nodes.text: Arming in STAY Mode 2

nodes.title: BOSCH  Copyright Notice  New Zealand Telepermit Notes
nodes.text: Hold down the [0] button until two beeps sound. The STAY indicator lights and exit time starts counting.

nodes.title: BOSCH  Copyright Notice  New Zealand Telepermit Notes
nodes.text: Any zones programmed to be automatically isolated in STAY Mode 2 flash until exit time expires. At the end of exit time, all zones selected to be automatically isolated extinguish and the codepad provides one short beep.

nodes.title: BOSCH  Copyright Notice  New Zealand Telepermit Notes
nodes.text: 5.4 Programming STAY Mode 2 Zones

nodes.title: BOSCH  Copyright Notice  New Zealand Telepermit Notes
nodes.text: You can only program zones to be automatically isolated in STAY Mode 2 if you have a Master Code.

nodes.title: BOSCH  Copyright Notice  New Zealand Telepermit Notes
nodes.section: How to Program STAY Mode 2 Zones
nodes.text: How to Program STAY Mode 2 Zones

nodes.title: BOSCH  Copyright Notice  New Zealand Telepermit Notes
nodes.section: How to Program STAY Mode 2 Zones
nodes.text:
1. Enter your four-character Master Code, followed by the [4] and [#] keys (for example, $[ 2 ~ 5 ~ 8 ~ 0 ~ 4 ~ \# ] \rangle$ ). Three beeps sound and the STAY indicator flashes.   
2. Enter the zone number to be automatically isolated, followed by the $[ { ^ * } ]$ key (for example, $[ 1 \ ^ { * } ] = \mathrm { Z o n e \ 1 }$ , $[ 2 \ ^ { * } ] = \mathrm { Z o n e \ 2 }$ ). The selected zone flashes. If you make a mistake, enter the same zone number followed by the [#] key to clear the incorrect zone. To select additional zones to be automatically isolated in STAY Mode 2, repeat Step 2 as many times as required.   
3. To exit this mode, press the [#] key when you have selected all zones to be automatically isolated in STAY Mode 2. Two beeps sound and the STAY and AWAY indicators turn dark.

nodes.title: BOSCH  Copyright Notice  New Zealand Telepermit Notes
nodes.text: 6. Disarming the System

nodes.title: BOSCH  Copyright Notice  New Zealand Telepermit Notes
nodes.text: When you enter the premises after the system is armed in AWAY Mode, or if you have armed the system in STAY Mode 1 or STAY Mode 2, you must disarm the system before entry time expires to disable detection devices that activate an alarm. Only your installer can program the entry time.

nodes.title: BOSCH  Copyright Notice  New Zealand Telepermit Notes
nodes.text: If there was an alarm condition prior to disarming the system, a flashing zone indicator displays indicating a previous alarm on that zone.

nodes.title: BOSCH  Copyright Notice  New Zealand Telepermit Notes
nodes.text: How to Disarm the System

nodes.title: BOSCH  Copyright Notice  New Zealand Telepermit Notes
nodes.text: Enter your user code followed by the [#] key (for example, [2 5 8 0 #]). Two beeps sound.

nodes.title: BOSCH  Copyright Notice  New Zealand Telepermit Notes
nodes.text: 7. User Codes

nodes.title: BOSCH  Copyright Notice  New Zealand Telepermit Notes
nodes.text: 7.1 Adding User Codes

nodes.title: BOSCH  Copyright Notice  New Zealand Telepermit Notes
nodes.text: Only the Master Code holder can add or change other system user codes, including the Master Code. Up to eight user codes can be programmed to operate the system.

nodes.title: BOSCH  Copyright Notice  New Zealand Telepermit Notes
nodes.section: How to Add a User Code
nodes.text: How to Add a User Code

nodes.title: BOSCH  Copyright Notice  New Zealand Telepermit Notes
nodes.section: How to Add a User Code
nodes.text:
1. Enter your four-character Master Code, followed by [1] and [#] (for example, [2 5 8 0 1 #]). Three beeps sound and the STAY and AWAY indicators flash.   
2. Enter the user code number (1 to 8) followed by the [#] key (for example, $[ 2 \# ] = \operatorname { U s e r } 2$ , $[ 8 \# ] =$ User 8). Two beeps sound and the selected user number displays on the codepad indicators.   
3. Enter the digits required for the new code followed by the [#] key (for example, for user code 5768, enter $\left[ 5 7 6 8 \# \right]$ ). Two beeps sound and the STAY and AWAY indicators turn dark. To add or change other user codes, repeat this procedure as many times as required.

nodes.title: BOSCH  Copyright Notice  New Zealand Telepermit Notes
nodes.text: 7.2 Adding Radio Remote User Codes

nodes.title: BOSCH  Copyright Notice  New Zealand Telepermit Notes
nodes.text: Only the Master Code holder can add or change other system user codes, including the Master Code. Up to eight radio user codes (User Codes 9 to 16) can be programmed to operate the system.

nodes.title: BOSCH  Copyright Notice  New Zealand Telepermit Notes
nodes.section: How to Add a Radio Remote User Code
nodes.text: How to Add a Radio Remote User Code

nodes.title: BOSCH  Copyright Notice  New Zealand Telepermit Notes
nodes.section: How to Add a Radio Remote User Code
nodes.text:
1. Enter your four-character Master Code, followed by the [1] and [#] keys (for example, [2 5 8 0 1 #]). Three beeps sound and the STAY and AWAY indicators flash.   
2. Enter the radio remote user code number (9 to 16), followed by the [#] key (for example, $[ 9 \# ] =$ User 9, $[ 1 6 \# ] = \mathrm { U s e r } 1 6$ ). Two beeps sound and the selected user number displays on the codepad indicators.   
3. Press any button on the keyfob so the system learns the ID number. Two beeps sound and the STAY and AWAY indicators extinguish. To add or change other radio remote user codes, repeat this procedure as many times as required.

nodes.title: BOSCH  Copyright Notice  New Zealand Telepermit Notes
nodes.text: 7.3 Deleting User Codes/Radio User Codes

nodes.title: BOSCH  Copyright Notice  New Zealand Telepermit Notes
nodes.text: Only the Master Code holder can delete other system user codes.

nodes.title: BOSCH  Copyright Notice  New Zealand Telepermit Notes
nodes.section: How to Delete a User Code
nodes.text: How to Delete a User Code

nodes.title: BOSCH  Copyright Notice  New Zealand Telepermit Notes
nodes.section: How to Delete a User Code
nodes.text:
1. Enter your four-character Master Code, followed by the [1] and $[ \# ]$ keys (for example, $[ 2 \ 5 \ 8 \ 0 \ 1 \ \# ] ,$ ). Three beeps sound and the STAY and AWAY indicators flash.   
2. Enter the user code number (User Code 1 to 8, Radio User Code 9 to 16), followed by the [#] key (for example, $[ 2 \# ] = \operatorname { U s e r } 2$ , $[ 1 6 \# ] = \mathrm { U s e r }$ 16). Two beeps sound and the selected user number displays on the codepad indicators.   
3. Press the [\*] key to delete the selected user code. Two beeps sound and the STAY and AWAY indicators turn dark. To delete other user codes, repeat this procedure as many times as required.

nodes.text: 9. Alarms

nodes.title: BOSCH  Copyright Notice  New Zealand Telepermit Notes
nodes.text: 9.1 Duress Alarm

nodes.title: BOSCH  Copyright Notice  New Zealand Telepermit Notes
nodes.text: A codepad duress alarm is used as a silent hold-up alarm. This only occurs when the number 9 is added to the end of any valid user code used to disarm the system (for example, [2 5 8 0 9 #]). A duress alarm is only useful if your system reports back to a monitoring station or pocket pager, because domestic reporting (such as a mobile phone) cannot decipher which type of alarm occurred.

nodes.text: 9.3 Fire Alarm

nodes.text: The horn speaker emits a distinct fire sound when both the [4] and [6] keys are pressed simultaneously. Contact your installer to disable the ability to activate the codepad fire alarm or to silence the codepad fire alarm.

nodes.title: BOSCH  Copyright Notice  New Zealand Telepermit Notes
nodes.text: 9.5 Tamper Alarm (Access Denied)

nodes.title: BOSCH  Copyright Notice  New Zealand Telepermit Notes
nodes.text: The tamper alarm restricts the number of times an invalid user code can be used in an attempt to operate the system. When the number of incorrect code attempts equals the number programmed by your installer, the system activates an alarm condition. If reporting back to a security monitoring station, the system sends an Access Denied Report.

nodes.title: BOSCH  Copyright Notice  New Zealand Telepermit Notes
nodes.text: To shutdown and lockout a codepad for a period of time (0 to 150 seconds), ask your installer to program this feature.

nodes.title: BOSCH  Copyright Notice  New Zealand Telepermit Notes
nodes.text: 10. Isolating Zones

nodes.title: BOSCH  Copyright Notice  New Zealand Telepermit Notes
nodes.text: Isolating zones allow you to manually disable one or more zones before arming the system. Once a zone is isolated, you can access that zone during the armed state without activating an alarm.

nodes.title: BOSCH  Copyright Notice  New Zealand Telepermit Notes
nodes.text: For example, you may need to isolate a zone because before arming the system a PIR detector might generate a false alarm, or you need to leave a pet inside a particular zone while away.

nodes.title: BOSCH  Copyright Notice  New Zealand Telepermit Notes
nodes.text: Isolating zones is performed by one of two methods. Method two is optional and only allows those user codes programmed by your installer access to isolate zones.

nodes.title: BOSCH  Copyright Notice  New Zealand Telepermit Notes
nodes.text: 10.1 Standard Isolating

nodes.title: BOSCH  Copyright Notice  New Zealand Telepermit Notes
nodes.text: Standard Isolating allows all operators to isolate zones without knowing a valid user code.

nodes.title: BOSCH  Copyright Notice  New Zealand Telepermit Notes
nodes.text: How to Isolate a Zone

nodes.title: BOSCH  Copyright Notice  New Zealand Telepermit Notes
nodes.text:
1. Press the [\*] key twice to enter Isolating Mode. Three beeps sound and the STAY indicator flashes.   
2. Enter the zone number (1 to 8), followed by the [\*] key (for example, $[ 1 \ ^ { * } ] = \mathrm { Z o n e \ 1 }$ , $[ 2 ^ { * } ] =$ Zone 2). Each zone to isolate has a corresponding zone indicator that flashes. If you selected an incorrect zone to isolate, enter the incorrect zone number again followed by the [\*] key. Repeat Step 2 if you are isolating more than one zone, until all zones to isolate are selected.

nodes.title: BOSCH  Copyright Notice  New Zealand Telepermit Notes
nodes.text: 3. Press the [#] key after all selected zones are isolated.

nodes.title: BOSCH  Copyright Notice  New Zealand Telepermit Notes
nodes.text: Two beeps sound and the system returns to the disarmed state.

nodes.title: BOSCH  Copyright Notice  New Zealand Telepermit Notes
nodes.text: 10.2 Code to Isolate

nodes.title: BOSCH  Copyright Notice  New Zealand Telepermit Notes
nodes.text: Only those user codes with the Code to Isolate priority level can isolate zones. If any user code has this priority level, the standard isolating method (see Section 10.1 Standard Isolating) does not function.

nodes.title: BOSCH  Copyright Notice  New Zealand Telepermit Notes
nodes.text: How to Isolate a Zone

nodes.title: BOSCH  Copyright Notice  New Zealand Telepermit Notes
nodes.text:
1. Press the [\*] key followed by your user code and the $[ { ^ * } ]$ key again to enter Isolating Mode (for example, $[ ^ { * } 2 5 8 0 ^ { * } ] )$ ). Three beeps sound and the STAY indicator flashes.   
2. Enter the zone number (1 to 8), followed by the [\*] key (for example, $[ 1 \ ^ { * } ] = \mathrm { Z o n e \ 1 } ,$ $[ 2 ^ { * } ] =$ Zone 2). Each zone to isolate has a corresponding zone indicator that flashes. If you selected an incorrect zone to isolate, enter the incorrect zone number again followed by the [\*] key. Repeat Step 2, if isolating more than one zone, until all zones to isolate are selected.   
3. Press the [#] key after all selected zones are isolated. Two beeps sound and the system returns to the disarmed state.

nodes.text: 11. Setting the Date and Time

nodes.title: BOSCH  Copyright Notice  New Zealand Telepermit Notes
nodes.text: Programming the date and time is only required when you need functions such as automatic test reports, automatic arming, and history events to operate correctly.

nodes.section: How to Program Date and Time
nodes.text: How to Program Date and Time

nodes.title: BOSCH  Copyright Notice  New Zealand Telepermit Notes
nodes.section: How to Program Date and Time
nodes.text:
1. Enter your Master Code followed by the [6] and [#] keys (for example, $[ 2 \ : 5 \ : 8 \ : 0 \ : 6 \ : \# ] _ { . }$ ). Three beeps sound and the STAY and AWAY indicators flash.   
2. Enter the day, month, year, hour, and minute using the (DD, MM, YY, HH, MM) format (that is, $\mathrm { D D } = \mathrm { d a y }$ of the month, $\mathbf { M M } =$ month of the year, $\mathrm { Y Y = }$ current year, $\mathrm { H H } =$ hour of the day, $\mathbf { M M } =$ minute of the day).

nodes.text: 12. Fault Analysis Mode

nodes.title: BOSCH  Copyright Notice  New Zealand Telepermit Notes
nodes.text: If a fault occurs, the FAULT or MAINS indicators flash and the codepad beeps once every minute.

nodes.title: BOSCH  Copyright Notice  New Zealand Telepermit Notes
nodes.text: 12.1 AC Fail

nodes.title: BOSCH  Copyright Notice  New Zealand Telepermit Notes
nodes.text: If the AC mains supply fails, the MAINS indicator flashes until the AC mains supply is restored. Pressing the [#] key once acknowledges the fault and stops the codepad from beeping once every minute.

nodes.title: BOSCH  Copyright Notice  New Zealand Telepermit Notes
nodes.text: 12.2 System Faults

nodes.title: BOSCH  Copyright Notice  New Zealand Telepermit Notes
nodes.section: How to Determine the Type of System Fault
nodes.text: How to Determine the Type of System Fault

nodes.title: BOSCH  Copyright Notice  New Zealand Telepermit Notes
nodes.section: How to Determine the Type of System Fault
nodes.text: To determine all system faults other than the AC mains supply, enter Fault Analysis Mode:

nodes.title: BOSCH  Copyright Notice  New Zealand Telepermit Notes
nodes.section: How to Determine the Type of System Fault
nodes.text:
1. Hold down the [5] key until two beeps sound. The FAULT indicator lights steadily and the STAY and AWAY indicators flash in unison. Any zone indicators displayed indicate the type of fault that occurred. See Table 10 for the list of system faults that can occur.   
2. To further determine the type of fault condition, hold down the key that corresponds to the zone indicator displayed.   
3. To exit Fault Analysis Mode and return to the disarmed state, press the [#] key. The FAULT indicator remains displayed and the codepad stops beeping once per minute.

Zone LED 1 indicates 'FAULT Condition' (a general indicator), Zone 2 indicates 'Battery Fail', Zone 3 indicates 'Sensor Watch', Zone 4 indicates 'Horn Speaker Fail', Zone 5 indicates 'Telephone Line Fail', Zone 6 indicates 'E2 Fault', and Zones 7 and 8 jointly indicate 'Fuse Fail' and 'Communication Fail'. This table is critical for diagnosing faults during Fault Analysis Mode (Section 12.1), where users hold the [5] key to trigger fault indicators. The table enables technicians to quickly identify and resolve issues like low battery, sensor malfunctions, or communication failures. It also aligns with surrounding sections discussing system arming, zone isolation, and alarm configurations, reinforcing how fault detection integrates into overall system reliability and user troubleshooting workflows.

nodes.title: BOSCH  Copyright Notice  New Zealand Telepermit Notes
nodes.text: Battery Fail

nodes.title: BOSCH  Copyright Notice  New Zealand Telepermit Notes
nodes.text: A battery fail fault registers when the system detects a low capacity back-up battery. The system automatically performs a Battery Test every 4 hours and every time the system is armed.

nodes.title: BOSCH  Copyright Notice  New Zealand Telepermit Notes
nodes.text: Date and Time

nodes.title: BOSCH  Copyright Notice  New Zealand Telepermit Notes
nodes.text: The date and time fault registers every time the system powers down. This type of fault does not cause the FAULT indicator to display on the codepad unless your installer has programmed the automatic arming time. See Section 11. Setting the Date and Time to program the date and time.

nodes.title: BOSCH  Copyright Notice  New Zealand Telepermit Notes
nodes.text: Sensor Watch Fail

nodes.title: BOSCH  Copyright Notice  New Zealand Telepermit Notes
nodes.text: A sensor watch fault registers because one or more detection devices failed to notice any movement during the disarmed state for the time period programmed by your installer. The fault clears when the zone in question detects movement and resets.

nodes.title: BOSCH  Copyright Notice  New Zealand Telepermit Notes
nodes.text: While in Fault Analysis Mode, hold down the [5] key until two beeps sound. The indicator lights that corresponds to the faulted zone.

nodes.title: BOSCH  Copyright Notice  New Zealand Telepermit Notes
nodes.text: Horn Speaker Fail

nodes.title: BOSCH  Copyright Notice  New Zealand Telepermit Notes
nodes.text: A horn speaker failure fault registers when the system detects the horn speaker is disconnected. This fault clears once the horn speaker is reconnected. Your installer needs to program the system for this feature to operate.

nodes.title: BOSCH  Copyright Notice  New Zealand Telepermit Notes
nodes.text: Telephone Line Fail

nodes.title: BOSCH  Copyright Notice  New Zealand Telepermit Notes
nodes.text: A telephone line failure fault registers when the system detects the telephone line is disconnected from the control panel. Your installer needs to program the system for this feature to operate.

nodes.title: BOSCH  Copyright Notice  New Zealand Telepermit Notes
nodes.text: E2 Fault

nodes.title: BOSCH  Copyright Notice  New Zealand Telepermit Notes
nodes.text: An E2 failure fault registers when the system detects an internal checksum error. Contact your installer as soon as this fault displays.

nodes.title: BOSCH  Copyright Notice  New Zealand Telepermit Notes
nodes.text: Fuse Fail

nodes.title: BOSCH  Copyright Notice  New Zealand Telepermit Notes
nodes.text: A fuse failure fault occurs when either of the two 1 A fuses are blown. Contact your installer as soon as this fault displays.

nodes.title: BOSCH  Copyright Notice  New Zealand Telepermit Notes
nodes.text: Communication Fail

nodes.title: BOSCH  Copyright Notice  New Zealand Telepermit Notes
nodes.text: A communication fail fault registers when the control panel fails to communicate with the receiving party (for example, a monitoring company, mobile phone, pocket pager, and so on). The communication fault clears once the control panel successfully reports to the receiving party.

nodes.text: Use this feature to program the Telco Arm Sequence and Telco Disarm Sequence (Call Forward $\mathrm { O n } / \mathrm { O f f } )$ .

nodes.title: BOSCH  Copyright Notice  New Zealand Telepermit Notes
nodes.text: 13.1 Telco Arm Sequence

nodes.title: BOSCH  Copyright Notice  New Zealand Telepermit Notes
nodes.text: Use this to program the Call Forward – Immediate On sequence or Call Forward – No Answer sequence to automatically operate when you arm the system in AWAY Mode. This feature is only available if your telecommunications provider has the call-forward option.

nodes.title: BOSCH  Copyright Notice  New Zealand Telepermit Notes
nodes.text: The examples given in this feature are only applicable to Australia.

nodes.title: BOSCH  Copyright Notice  New Zealand Telepermit Notes
nodes.text: Call Forward – Immediate On

nodes.title: BOSCH  Copyright Notice  New Zealand Telepermit Notes
nodes.text: You can redirect calls to anywhere in Australia, including mobile phones, pagers, and answering services. When Call Forward is turned on, your telephone does not ring.

nodes.title: BOSCH  Copyright Notice  New Zealand Telepermit Notes
nodes.text: Call Forward – No Answer

nodes.title: BOSCH  Copyright Notice  New Zealand Telepermit Notes
nodes.text: When your telephone is not answered within 20 seconds, this feature redirects all incoming calls to another number anywhere in Australia, but you can still make outgoing calls.

The table is structured with two columns per row, pairing standard digits with their special programming equivalents. For example, the asterisk (*) is programmed as *1, the hash (#) as *2, a 4-second pause as *3, and a break as *4. This table directly supports Section 13 of the guide, which explains how to program call-forward sequences for arm/disarm operations. The table’s purpose is to standardize input syntax for telecom commands, enabling users to configure call-forwarding (e.g., *61 for No Answer, *21 for Immediate On) or disable sequences (e.g., *4 for break). The presence of special codes like *3 and *4 indicates that the system interprets pauses and breaks as control signals, which are essential for distinguishing between command sequences and phone numbers. This table is critical for users to correctly program or disable telecom functions without triggering unintended behavior, as misinterpretation of these codes could lead to failed configurations or system errors.

nodes.section: How to Program the Telco Arm Sequence
nodes.text: How to Program the Telco Arm Sequence

nodes.title: BOSCH  Copyright Notice  New Zealand Telepermit Notes
nodes.section: How to Program the Telco Arm Sequence
nodes.text:
1. Enter your four-character Master Code, followed by the [3] and [#] keys (for example, $[ \dot { 2 } \ 5 \ 8 \ 0 \ 3 \ \# ] ,$ ). Three beeps sound and the STAY and AWAY indicators flash.   
2. Press button [1] and [#] keys to select the Telco Arm Sequence. Three beeps sound.   
3. Enter the call forward sequence (for example, [\* 6 1][Phone Number][#] to program the Call Forward - No Answer sequence, or $[ * 2 1 ]$ [Phone Number][#] to program the Call Forward Immediate sequence). To program a “\*” in the Telco Arm Sequence, enter $[ * 1 ]$ . To program a “#” in the Telco Arm Sequence, enter $[ * 2 ]$ .   
4. Press the [#] key when finished. Two beeps sound, and the STAY and AWAY indicators go dark.

nodes.section: How to Program the Telco Arm Sequence
nodes.text: To disable the Telco Arm Sequence, enter the call forward sequence as [\* 4] (break) for Step 3.

nodes.text: 13.2 Telco Disarm Sequence

nodes.title: BOSCH  Copyright Notice  New Zealand Telepermit Notes
nodes.text: This feature automatically disables the call forward sequence when disarming the system.

nodes.title: BOSCH  Copyright Notice  New Zealand Telepermit Notes
nodes.section: How to Program the Telco Disarm Sequence
nodes.text: How to Program the Telco Disarm Sequence

nodes.title: BOSCH  Copyright Notice  New Zealand Telepermit Notes
nodes.section: How to Program the Telco Disarm Sequence
nodes.text:
1. Enter your four-character Master Code followed by the [3] and [#] keys (for example, $[ 2 ~ 5 ~ 8 ~ 0 ~ 3 ~ \# ] \rangle$ ). Three beeps sound and the STAY and AWAY indicators flash.   
2. Press the [2] and [#] key to select the Telco Disarm Sequence. Three beeps sound.   
3. Enter the call forward disable sequence (for example, [# 6 1 #] to disable the No Answer Call Forward sequence, or [# 2 1 #] to disable the Call Forward Immediate sequence). To program a “#” in the Telco Disarm Sequence, enter [\* 2].   
4. Press the [#] key when finished. Two beeps sound, and the STAY and AWAY indicators go dark.

nodes.section: How to Program the Telco Disarm Sequence
nodes.text: To disable the Telco Disarm Sequence, enter the call forward sequence as [\* 4] (break) for Step 3.

nodes.text: 14. Turning Outputs On/Off

nodes.title: BOSCH  Copyright Notice  New Zealand Telepermit Notes
nodes.text: This feature only applies if your installer set up an output that can be turned on or off by the codepad. The output programmed by your installer can control a pool pump, outside lighting, and so on. Up to three separate outputs may be programmed.

nodes.title: BOSCH  Copyright Notice  New Zealand Telepermit Notes
nodes.section: How to Turn an Output On or Off
nodes.text: How to Turn an Output On or Off

nodes.title: BOSCH  Copyright Notice  New Zealand Telepermit Notes
nodes.section: How to Turn an Output On or Off
nodes.text:
1. Enter your Master Code followed by the [5] and [#] keys (for example, [2 5 8 0 5 #]). Three beeps sound and the STAY and AWAY indicators flash.   
2. Enter the output number (1 to 3) that you wish to turn on or off.   
3. Press the [#] key to turn the output on, or press the [\*] key to turn the output off. Three beeps sound if the output is turned on, and two beeps sound if the output is turned off. Repeat Step 2 and Step 3 if you require more than one output to be turned on or off.   
4. Press the [#] key to exit this function. Two beeps sound and the STAY and AWAY indicators go dark.

nodes.title: BOSCH  Copyright Notice  New Zealand Telepermit Notes
nodes.text: 15. Reset Latching Outputs

nodes.title: BOSCH  Copyright Notice  New Zealand Telepermit Notes
nodes.text: This feature only applies if your installer programmed an output to latch (remain on) until you acknowledge the event that occurred.

nodes.title: BOSCH  Copyright Notice  New Zealand Telepermit Notes
nodes.text: How To Reset Latching Outputs

nodes.title: BOSCH  Copyright Notice  New Zealand Telepermit Notes
nodes.text: Hold down the [7] key until two beeps sound. The output resets.

nodes.text: 16. Codepad ID/Buzzer Tone Change

nodes.title: BOSCH  Copyright Notice  New Zealand Telepermit Notes
nodes.text: Hold down the [8] key continuously to change the tone of the codepad buzzer. There are 50 different tones, from $1 5 0 0 \ \mathrm { H z }$ to $5 0 0 0 \mathrm { H z }$ . If multiple codepads are installed, each codepad can sound a different tone.

nodes.text: 17. Testing

nodes.title: BOSCH  Copyright Notice  New Zealand Telepermit Notes
nodes.text: There are various functions for testing that your system is operating correctly.

nodes.title: BOSCH  Copyright Notice  New Zealand Telepermit Notes
nodes.text: 17.1 Horn Speaker Test

nodes.title: BOSCH  Copyright Notice  New Zealand Telepermit Notes
nodes.text:
Press and hold the [1] key until two beeps sound.   
The horn speaker sounds for 2 seconds.

nodes.title: BOSCH  Copyright Notice  New Zealand Telepermit Notes
nodes.text: 17.2 Bell Test

nodes.title: BOSCH  Copyright Notice  New Zealand Telepermit Notes
nodes.text:
Press and hold the [2] key until two beeps sound.   
The bell output operates for 2 seconds.

nodes.title: BOSCH  Copyright Notice  New Zealand Telepermit Notes
nodes.text: 17.3 Strobe Test

nodes.title: BOSCH  Copyright Notice  New Zealand Telepermit Notes
nodes.text:
1. Press and hold the [3] key until three beeps sound. The strobe flashes.   
2. Press and hold the [3] key until two beeps sound. The strobe stops flashing.

nodes.title: BOSCH  Copyright Notice  New Zealand Telepermit Notes
nodes.text: 17.4 Walk Test Mode

nodes.title: BOSCH  Copyright Notice  New Zealand Telepermit Notes
nodes.text: Use Walk Test Mode to test detection devices for proper operation. Every time you test a zone, the codepad sounds one long beep and the horn speaker sounds one short beep to indicate the zone was activated when testing.

nodes.title: BOSCH  Copyright Notice  New Zealand Telepermit Notes
nodes.text:
1. Enter your four-character Master Code, followed by the [7] and [#] keys (for example, $\left[ 2 \ 5 \ 8 \ 0 \ 7 \ \# \right] )$ . Three beeps sound, and the STAY and AWAY indicators flash. The codepad beeps once every second while the system is in Walk Test Mode.   
2. Activate all zones that require testing. The codepad sounds one long beep and the horn speaker sounds one short beep every time a zone is faulted (unsealed) and restored.   
3. When you finish testing all required zones, press the [#] key to exit this mode. Two beeps sound, and the STAY and AWAY indicators turn off. The system returns to the disarmed state.

nodes.title: BOSCH  Copyright Notice  New Zealand Telepermit Notes
nodes.text: 17.5 Test Report

nodes.title: BOSCH  Copyright Notice  New Zealand Telepermit Notes
nodes.text: This feature only applies if your system reports by telephone. Press and hold the [9] key until two beeps sound. The system sends a Test Report without sounding the sirens.

nodes.text: Use this function to replay the last 40 events that occurred to the system. The event memory history replays all alarms and arming/disarming of the system in AWAY Mode, STAY Mode 1, and STAY Mode 2.

nodes.text: 19. Day Alarm

nodes.title: BOSCH  Copyright Notice  New Zealand Telepermit Notes
nodes.text: Day alarm allows a combination of zones to be monitored during the disarmed state by beeping the codepad buzzer. Only your installer can program zones 1 to 4 to operate for day alarm.

nodes.title: BOSCH  Copyright Notice  New Zealand Telepermit Notes
nodes.text: Example

nodes.title: BOSCH  Copyright Notice  New Zealand Telepermit Notes
nodes.text: A day alarm can be set up at the front door of a shop with a pressure mat or electronic beam that customers activate as they enter and exit the shop. As the customers walk onto the pressure mat or break the electronic beam, the codepad buzzer beeps.

nodes.title: BOSCH  Copyright Notice  New Zealand Telepermit Notes
nodes.section: How to Turn Day Alarm On
nodes.text: Hold down the [4] key until three beeps sound. Day alarm turns on. All zones programmed for day alarm operation cause the codepad buzzer to beep during the disarmed state when activated.

nodes.text: 20. Remote Arming By Telephone

nodes.title: BOSCH  Copyright Notice  New Zealand Telepermit Notes
nodes.text: Use this feature to arm your system from any remote location using a telephone. For security reasons, the system cannot be disarmed using this method. This feature requires a touch-tone telephone. Your installer must program this feature to operate.

nodes.title: BOSCH  Copyright Notice  New Zealand Telepermit Notes
nodes.section: How to Remotely Arm your System Using the Telephone
nodes.text: How to Remotely Arm your System Using the Telephone

nodes.title: BOSCH  Copyright Notice  New Zealand Telepermit Notes
nodes.section: How to Remotely Arm your System Using the Telephone
nodes.text:
1. Call the telephone number connected to your control panel.   
2. When the control panel answers the incoming call, a short jingle is heard. To arm the system, press the [\*] key on the touch-tone telephone for 1 to 3 seconds. If you hear modem tones when the control panel answers the incoming call, the system was programmed for remote programming functions by your installer. Wait for a pause between the tones before pressing the [\*] key. After releasing the [\*] key on the touch-tone telephone, two beeps sound indicating that the system was armed in AWAY Mode.   
3. Hang up the telephone and the system remains armed.

nodes.title: BOSCH  Copyright Notice  New Zealand Telepermit Notes
nodes.section: How to Remotely Arm your System Using the Telephone
nodes.text: If your installer programs answering machine bypass, you must call the control panel twice to make a connection with the system. For example, call the telephone number that your control panel is connected to, let the call ring no more than four rings, then hang up the telephone. Wait a minimum of 8 seconds before you call the control panel again.

nodes.text: 21. Domestic Dialling

nodes.title: BOSCH  Copyright Notice  New Zealand Telepermit Notes
nodes.text: Domestic dialling is used to call your mobile phone or a relative/friend in the event your control panel activates an alarm. Up to three different telephone numbers can be programmed for the control panel to call when an alarm occurs. Only your installer can set the system to report in the domestic format, however, the Master Code holder can change the domestic telephone numbers at any time.

nodes.title: BOSCH  Copyright Notice  New Zealand Telepermit Notes
nodes.text: 21.1 Acknowledging Domestic Calls

nodes.title: BOSCH  Copyright Notice  New Zealand Telepermit Notes
nodes.text: When an alarm condition occurs, the system calls the first telephone number that was programmed. When you answer an incoming call, you hear the system sound a repeating siren tone followed by a pause, continually for 2 minutes (for example, siren tone, pause, siren tone, and pause).

nodes.title: BOSCH  Copyright Notice  New Zealand Telepermit Notes
nodes.text: If you do not acknowledge the call from the control panel during a pause between siren tones, the control panel hangs up after 2 minutes expire, and calls the next telephone number.

nodes.title: BOSCH  Copyright Notice  New Zealand Telepermit Notes
nodes.text: Pressing the $[ { ^ * } ]$ key for 1 to 3 seconds during the pause acknowledges the call and no further calls are made for that event. If the call is successfully acknowledged, a tone of decreasing pitch is heard.

The table is structured to show how specific digits (0–9, *, #, and special sequences like *4 or *3) correspond to actions such as entering programming mode, inserting breaks between phone numbers, or triggering system functions. Notably, the table shows that digit '3' maps to '*', '4' to '#', '6' to 'break', and '7' to '7', while '5' is associated with a 4-second pause. This enables the system to distinguish between data (phone digits) and control signals (programming commands), which is critical for correctly programming up to three phone numbers for alarm notifications. The table’s content is tightly integrated with the procedural instructions for domestic dialling, ensuring operators can accurately input phone numbers while understanding how to insert breaks or pauses without confusing the system.

nodes.title: BOSCH  Copyright Notice  New Zealand Telepermit Notes
nodes.text: 21.2 Programming Domestic Telephone Numbers

nodes.title: BOSCH  Copyright Notice  New Zealand Telepermit Notes
nodes.text: If your system is configured for domestic dialling, this function allows any Master Code holder to program telephone numbers the control panel calls in the event of an alarm.

nodes.title: BOSCH  Copyright Notice  New Zealand Telepermit Notes
nodes.text: How to Program Telephone Numbers

nodes.title: BOSCH  Copyright Notice  New Zealand Telepermit Notes
nodes.text:
1. Enter your four-character Master Code, followed by the [2] and [#] keys (for example, [2 5 8 0 2 #]). Three beeps sound and the STAY and AWAY indicators flash. If there are telephone numbers already programmed, they are displayed one digit at a time by the codepad indicators. If there are no telephone numbers programmed, a further two beeps sound after entering this mode. These two beeps are normally heard after the last digit of the last telephone number displays.   
2. Enter all digits for the first telephone number (for example, [9 6 7 2 1 7 1 7]). As each digit is entered, the corresponding codepad indicators display.   
3. If there is more than one telephone number to be programmed, press [\* 4]. This inserts a break between the first telephone number and the second telephone number. If there is only one telephone number to program, press the [#] key to exit this function.   
4. Enter all the digits of the second telephone number (for example, [9 6 7 2 1 0 5 5]). As each digit is entered, the corresponding codepad indicators display.   
5. After the last digit of the second telephone number is programmed, press the [#] key to exit this function unless a third telephone number is required. If there is a third telephone number to program, press the [\* 4] button to insert a break between the second telephone number and the third telephone number.

nodes.text: 21.3 Disable Domestic Dialling

nodes.title: BOSCH  Copyright Notice  New Zealand Telepermit Notes
nodes.text: To cancel domestic dialling (for example, you are moving and do not want the system to continue calling your mobile phone), enter the following sequence.

nodes.title: BOSCH  Copyright Notice  New Zealand Telepermit Notes
nodes.text:
1. Enter your four-character Master Code, followed by the [2] and [#] keys (for example, $[ \dot { 2 } \ 5 \ 8 \ 0 \ 2 \ \# ] _ { . }$ ). Two beeps sound and the STAY and AWAY indicators flash.   
2. Press the [\*] button followed by the [4] and [#] keys (for example, $[ { ^ * } 4 \# ] )$ ). The STAY and AWAY indicators go dark.

nodes.text: 22. Partitioning

nodes.title: BOSCH  Copyright Notice  New Zealand Telepermit Notes
nodes.text: You can partition or split the Solution 880 Control Panel into two individual areas. You can operate both areas from one Master Partitioned codepad or from separate area addressable codepads.

nodes.title: BOSCH  Copyright Notice  New Zealand Telepermit Notes
nodes.text: 22.1 Master Partitioned Codepad Indicators

nodes.title: BOSCH  Copyright Notice  New Zealand Telepermit Notes

Captions: Figure 6: Master Partitioned Codepad 
Footnotes: None

Visual Analysis: The image presents a schematic diagram of a 'Master Partitioned Codepad' from Bosch Security Systems, as indicated by the brand name at the top. The diagram is a black-and-white illustration showing the layout of the control panel's indicator lights. It is organized into four horizontal sections. The top section contains eight rectangular indicator lights labeled 1 through 8, collectively identified as 'Zones'. Below this, there are two side-by-side sections: the left one contains four lights labeled 1 through 4 under 'Area On / Off', and the right one contains four lights labeled 1 through 4 under 'Area Display'. The bottom section displays four rectangular indicator lights labeled 'AUX', 'MAINS', 'FAULT', and 'PARTIAL'. All indicators are depicted as solid black rectangles, suggesting they are illuminated. The diagram is presented in a clean, technical style with clear labels and numerical identifiers, designed for instructional purposes. The surrounding text context explains that this codepad is used in a partitioned security system, where operations are context-dependent on which area's indicator is lit, and the indicators provide real-time status information for zones, areas, and system health.

nodes.title: BOSCH  Copyright Notice  New Zealand Telepermit Notes
nodes.text: The indicators on a Master Partitioned codepad are configured into four groups. The following paragraphs describe the indicators.

nodes.title: BOSCH  Copyright Notice  New Zealand Telepermit Notes
nodes.text: 22.1.1 Zone Indicators

nodes.title: BOSCH  Copyright Notice  New Zealand Telepermit Notes
nodes.text: The zone indicators (1 to 8) display the status of each zone. These zones belong to the area whose AREA DISPLAY indicator is lit. If a ZONE indicator is lit, that zone is unsealed. If a ZONE indicator is not lit, that zone is sealed.

nodes.title: BOSCH  Copyright Notice  New Zealand Telepermit Notes
nodes.text: 22.1.2 Area On/Off Indicators

nodes.title: BOSCH  Copyright Notice  New Zealand Telepermit Notes
nodes.text: The group of four AREA ON/OFF DISPLAY indicators show the status of each area. If an indicator is lit, that area is armed. If the indicator is not lit, that area is disarmed.

nodes.title: BOSCH  Copyright Notice  New Zealand Telepermit Notes
nodes.text: 22.1.3 Area Display Indicators

nodes.title: BOSCH  Copyright Notice  New Zealand Telepermit Notes
nodes.text: A group of four AREA DISPLAY indicators determine the area to which the displayed zones belong.

nodes.title: BOSCH  Copyright Notice  New Zealand Telepermit Notes
nodes.text: 22.1.4 Status Indicators

nodes.title: BOSCH  Copyright Notice  New Zealand Telepermit Notes
nodes.text: This group of four indicators shows the following:

nodes.title: BOSCH  Copyright Notice  New Zealand Telepermit Notes
nodes.text: AUX Indicator

nodes.title: BOSCH  Copyright Notice  New Zealand Telepermit Notes
nodes.text: The AUX indicator displays when the system is using the telephone line to communicate to the receiving party.

nodes.title: BOSCH  Copyright Notice  New Zealand Telepermit Notes
nodes.text: The AUX indicator flashes in conjunction with the PARTIAL indicator to show successful entry into any programming mode. For example, this occurs when you are using Master Code functions.

nodes.title: BOSCH  Copyright Notice  New Zealand Telepermit Notes
nodes.text: Mains Indicator

nodes.title: BOSCH  Copyright Notice  New Zealand Telepermit Notes
nodes.text: This indicator displays the status of the AC mains supply. The indicator lights steadily when the AC is normal and flashes when there is an AC supply failure.

nodes.title: BOSCH  Copyright Notice  New Zealand Telepermit Notes
nodes.text: Fault Indicator

nodes.title: BOSCH  Copyright Notice  New Zealand Telepermit Notes
nodes.text: This indicator displays the status of the system’s fault register. If the FAULT indicator flashes when the system detects a fault that has not yet been acknowledged. If the indicator lights steadily, the fault has been acknowledged.

nodes.title: BOSCH  Copyright Notice  New Zealand Telepermit Notes
nodes.text: Partial Indicator

nodes.title: BOSCH  Copyright Notice  New Zealand Telepermit Notes
nodes.text: This indicator shows whether an area is armed in STAY Mode 1. If the PARTIAL indicator is lit, the area is armed in STAY Mode 1. If the indicator is not lit, no areas are armed in STAY Mode 1. When isolating zones, the PARTIAL indicator flashes to indicate that you are in the isolate mode. The PARTIAL indicator also flashes in conjunction with the AUX indicator to indicate successful entry into any programming mode (for example, when using Master Code functions).

nodes.section: 22.2 Operating From A Master Partitioned Codepad
nodes.text: 22.2 Operating From A Master Partitioned Codepad

nodes.title: BOSCH  Copyright Notice  New Zealand Telepermit Notes
nodes.section: 22.2 Operating From A Master Partitioned Codepad
nodes.text: If you have a partitioned system with a Master Partitioned codepad installed, operating procedures described throughout this guide are the same with one exception. All operations are relative to the area whose AREA DISPLAY indicator is illuminated at the time.

nodes.title: BOSCH  Copyright Notice  New Zealand Telepermit Notes
nodes.text: Example

nodes.title: BOSCH  Copyright Notice  New Zealand Telepermit Notes
nodes.text: When the AREA DISPLAY indicator number 2 is lit, all operations performed affect only Area 2. To perform operations in another area, you must move the AREA DISPLAY illuminator to the desired area.

nodes.title: BOSCH  Copyright Notice  New Zealand Telepermit Notes
nodes.section: To Move From One Area To The Next
nodes.text: To Move From One Area To The Next

nodes.title: BOSCH  Copyright Notice  New Zealand Telepermit Notes
nodes.section: To Move From One Area To The Next
nodes.text: Press the AWAY button.

nodes.title: BOSCH  Copyright Notice  New Zealand Telepermit Notes
nodes.section: To Move From One Area To The Next
nodes.text:
The area display indicator moves to the next area.   
Repeat until the desired indicator is lit.

nodes.title: BOSCH  Copyright Notice  New Zealand Telepermit Notes
nodes.text: 22.3 Operating From Area Addressable Codepads

nodes.title: BOSCH  Copyright Notice  New Zealand Telepermit Notes
nodes.text: If you have a partitioned system with Area Addressable codepads, the operating procedures described throughout this guide are the same. Refer to 16. Codepad ID/Buzzer Tone Change on page 14 to determine the area to which a particular codepad belongs.

nodes.text: 23. Basic Pager Reporting

nodes.title: BOSCH  Copyright Notice  New Zealand Telepermit Notes
nodes.text: This feature only applies if your system reports to a pocket pager. Basic pager reporting requires some interpretation of the numbers that appear on the display. It is possible to differentiate between 1000 different systems when a number of control panels report to the one pocket pager.

nodes.title: BOSCH  Copyright Notice  New Zealand Telepermit Notes
nodes.text: Subscriber ID Number

nodes.title: BOSCH  Copyright Notice  New Zealand Telepermit Notes
nodes.text: This is the identification number of the control panel and can only be programmed by your installer.

nodes.title: BOSCH  Copyright Notice  New Zealand Telepermit Notes
nodes.text: Zone Status

nodes.title: BOSCH  Copyright Notice  New Zealand Telepermit Notes
nodes.text: The zone status display shows you the status of each zone (1 to 8). Table 13 describes what each number means when displayed on the zone status display.

nodes.title: BOSCH  Copyright Notice  New Zealand Telepermit Notes
nodes.text:
Table 13: Zone Status Display Descriptions
Number DisplayedZone Description
0Zone Normal Indicates the corresponding zone is in the sealed state.
1Alarm Indicates the corresponding zone is unsealed and in alarm condition.
2Zone Bypassed Indicates a system operator manually isolated the corresponding zone. See Section 10. Isolating Zones for information on how to manually isolate a
3zone(s) prior to arming the system. Zone Trouble Indicates a zone was left unsealed after the end of exit time.

Table 13: Zone Status Display Descriptions
Number DisplayedZone Description
0Zone Normal Indicates the corresponding zone is in the sealed state.
1Alarm Indicates the corresponding zone is unsealed and in alarm condition.
2Zone Bypassed Indicates a system operator manually isolated the corresponding zone. See Section 10. Isolating Zones for information on how to manually isolate a
3zone(s) prior to arming the system. Zone Trouble Indicates a zone was left unsealed after the end of exit time.
Footnotes: None Analysis: Table 13 defines the numeric codes displayed on the Zone Status portion of the pager report, directly correlating to the physical zone indicators (1–8) described in Section 22.1.1. The table maps numeric outputs (0–3) to zone states: '0' indicates sealed (normal), '1' indicates alarm (unsealed and active), '2' indicates bypassed (manually isolated, as referenced to Section 10), and '3' indicates trouble (unsealed after exit time). These codes are part of the system’s communication protocol for remote monitoring via pager, where the Subscriber ID, Zone Status, and System Status are segmented into 4-digit codes (as per Table 14 on page 18). The table reinforces the physical indicator logic: lit ZONE indicators = unsealed, unlit = sealed. It supports the concept of partitioned operation (Section 22.2) by providing a standardized way to interpret zone status regardless of which area is active, as indicated by the AREA DISPLAY. The 'Zone Bypassed' state (code 2) is specifically tied to isolation procedures, which are critical during arming to avoid false alarms, and the 'Zone Trouble' state (code 3) signals a potential security lapse, requiring operator attention. This table is essential for operators to interpret remote alerts and maintain system integrity, especially in multi-area systems.

nodes.title: BOSCH  Copyright Notice  New Zealand Telepermit Notes

nodes.text:

Table 14: System Status
System StatusDescription Display
First digitIndicates whether the system is armed or disarmed: 8 = Disarmed
Second digit9 = Armed Indicates which codepad alarm was triggered by the operator: 0 = No Codepad Alarm 1 = Codepad Panic or Duress Alarm
Third digit2= Codepad Fire Alarm 3= Codepad Medical Alarm Indicates when the AC mains supply fails: 0 = AC Supply is normal
Fourth digit1 = AC Supply failed Indicates when a system fault occurs at the control panel: O = System Normal - There are no faults. 1= System Fault -There is a fault registered by the control panel.

Figure 7 also displays zone 3 is manually isolated and the system is armed. Structure:
Table 14: System Status
System StatusDescription Display
First digitIndicates whether the system is armed or disarmed: 8 = Disarmed
Second digit9 = Armed Indicates which codepad alarm was triggered by the operator: 0 = No Codepad Alarm 1 = Codepad Panic or Duress Alarm

Footnotes: None Analysis: Table 14, titled 'System Status,' details the four-digit code used in pager reporting to convey system operational status. The first digit indicates armed/disarmed state (8 = disarmed), second digit shows alarm type (9 = armed, 1 = panic/duress), third digit denotes fire/medical alarm or AC status (2 = fire, 3 = medical, 0 = AC normal), and fourth digit reports AC or system fault (0 = normal, 1 = fault). This table directly supports the context of pager reporting (Section 23) by decoding system status digits. It aligns with the partitioning context (Section 22) by providing system-wide status independent of area selection, as the pager message reflects global system state. The table clarifies how operators interpret pager messages, such as identifying armed status (9) or system faults (1), which is critical for troubleshooting and responding to security events. The table’s structure enables quick interpretation of multi-digit status codes, directly supporting the guide’s goal of simplifying system monitoring via pager.

nodes.title: Measuring happiness increases happiness  Abstract  Introduction
nodes.text: Abstract

nodes.title: Measuring happiness increases happiness  Abstract  Introduction
nodes.text: Happiness has been an overarching goal of mankind at least since Aristotle spoke of Eudaimonia. However measuring happiness has been elusive and until now has almost exclusively been done by asking survey questions about self-perceived happiness. We propose a novel approach, tracking happiness and stress through changes in body signals with a smartwatch, the “Happimeter”. It predicts individual emotions from sensor data collected by an Android Wear smartwatch, such as acceleration, heartbeat, and activity. The Happimeter was used over three months in the innovation lab of a bank with 22 employees to measure individual happiness, activity, and stress. The participants were randomly divided into an experimental and a control group of similar size. Both groups wore the watch and entered their subjective happiness, activity and stress levels several times a day. The user-entered ratings were then used to train a machine learning system using the sensors of the smartwatch to subsequently automatically predict happiness, activity, and stress. The experimental group received ongoing feedback about their mood and which activity, sensor signals, or other people, made them happier or unhappier, while the control group did not get any feedback about their predicted and manually entered emotions. Just like in quantum physics we observed a “Heisenberg Efect”, where the participants made aware of their measurements changed their behavior: Members of the experimental group that received happiness feedback were $1 6 \%$ happier, and $2 6 \%$ more active than the control group at the end of the experiment. No efect was observed for stress.

nodes.title: Measuring happiness increases happiness  Abstract  Introduction
nodes.text: Introduction

nodes.title: Measuring happiness increases happiness  Abstract  Introduction
nodes.text: Most people think they know when they are happy, sad, or stressed. However, emotional awareness is far from given [1]. People are notoriously bad of recognizing when they are sad or stressed. Being aware of one’s own emotions is of great help in coping with the challenges of daily life. Fear gets the driver on the highway to slam on the brakes when the truck is getting too close, but it can also be a powerful inhibitor when there is no reason to be fearful [2]. On the positive emotional side, striving for happiness is one of the biggest and most important goals of human beings [3]. In general, happiness increases productivity [4], work performance [5], career success [6] as well as health and other social factors [6]. On the other hand, unhappiness hampers efciency because employees start acting sloppily [4]. Further, a negative mood can lower expectancy, instrumentality, and valence for rewards and thus lead to a worse work performance [7].

nodes.title: Measuring happiness increases happiness  Abstract  Introduction
nodes.text: But how do we know when we are happy? Previous studies mainly surveyed and interviewed individuals in order to access their overall well-being [5, 6, 8]. However, all of these approaches sufer from problems of self-assessment and cognitive bias [9]. Further, such methods are not only time-consuming and expensive, but they also lack the ability of real-time analysis and actions.

nodes.title: Measuring happiness increases happiness  Abstract  Introduction
nodes.text: A system is required which automatically tracks the mood of a person at any time of the day to circumvent these limitations of surveys and interviews. Thanks to the rise of wearable sensor technologies such as smartwatches and wristbands, we get access to the most important source of emotional information: the body. Not only do smartwatches count the steps and give immediate feedback to the wearer on the display, but their built-in sensors access body and context information like heart rate, noise, or acceleration. Previous studies have shown that machine learning can be used to extract high-level features from body sensors that achieve high accuracy in diferent areas like activity recognition [10] or emotion recognition via an “Emotive Couch” [11]. Further, Blanchfower and Oswald [12] showed that physiological information i.e. blood pressure can be used to assess well-being. Thus, in this paper we introduce an alternative way to measure emotions through machine learning using body sensors from a smartwatch.

nodes.title: Measuring happiness increases happiness  Abstract  Introduction
nodes.text: To make individuals aware of their emotions and increase their well-being we employ a process called “virtual mirroring”. It has been introduced in [13], referring to a process in which individuals are shown metrics of their own communication behavior while they are told which communication behavior is desirable. In earlier work doing virtual mirroring by analyzing e-mail communication, it has been shown that individuals will change their behavior to be more collaborative, productive, and innovative [14]. Thus, through virtual mirroring organizations can enhance their performance and outcome.

nodes.title: Measuring happiness increases happiness  Abstract  Introduction
nodes.text: Heisenberg’s uncertainty principle states that two complementing characteristics, such as location and movement, cannot be determined simultaneously. Trying to measure a defnite position will make the measurement of the movement less accurate, and vice versa [15]. Gloor [16] has concluded that the same applies to humans. When a group of people is observed and if they know this, their self-refection is triggered which leads to a change in behavior. Furthermore, the measurement is not correct anymore due to people’s change in behavior.
